verdict.headline: High-risk freelance agreement that strips pre-existing IP, imposes a void 12-month non-compete, and delays pay indefinitely.
summary: The agreement transfers ownership of your own pre-existing tools and templates to the client upon signing without payment.
Payment terms permit unlimited unpaid revisions and delay payment for 90 days with no interest on late balances.
The contract allows the client to terminate at will with immediate effect while forfeiting all pay for work in progress.

findings.title: Immediate assignment of pre-existing materials
findings.quote: Freelancer dengan ini menyerahhakkan kepada Pelanggan, dengan jaminan hakmilik penuh, semua Hak Harta Intelek dalam Hasil Kerja dan dalam semua Bahan Sedia Ada, termasuk karya, alat, templat dan kod Freelancer yang sedia ada, sama ada atau tidak digunakan dalam projek, berkuat kuasa sebaik sahaja Perjanjian ini ditandatangani.
findings.why_risky: You permanently lose ownership of all your pre-existing tools, templates, and libraries upon signing, even before you are paid. Clause 4.2 reinforces this by barring any licence back to you, preventing you from using your own foundational tools or displaying the work in your portfolio.
findings.standard: Clients should only receive an assignment of or licence to the specific project deliverables upon full payment, while the freelancer retains all pre-existing tools, templates, and code.
findings.suggested_ask: Please limit the assignment to the deliverables once they are paid for, and confirm that I keep my pre-existing work, tools and templates, with a licence to you to use any that are built into the deliverables.

findings.title: Extended payment terms with discretionary sign-off

findings.why_risky: Payment is delayed for 90 days after written sign-off with no interest on late payments. Because clause 3.2 allows the client absolute discretion to demand unlimited revisions with no deemed acceptance timeline, the payment wait can be dragged out indefinitely.
findings.standard: Payment should be made within 14 to 30 days of invoice, accompanied by deemed acceptance within 7 to 14 days and interest on overdue balances.
findings.suggested_ask: Please pay within 30 days of invoice, treat the work as accepted if no written defects are raised within 10 days of delivery, and pay a kill fee for work done if the project is cancelled.

findings.why_risky: A 12-month post-termination restriction bars you from providing design or web development services to any other digital agency in Malaysia. Under Malaysian law, post-contractual restraints of trade are void, yet this clause exposes you to dispute risk. Section 28 has no general 'reasonable restraint' exception (only sale of goodwill and partnerships), so a shorter or paid restraint after the contract ends is not made valid; whether it reaches a non-solicitation clause is not settled.
findings.standard: Post-contractual non-compete clauses should not be imposed on freelancers, as ordinary confidentiality provisions adequately protect client business information.
findings.suggested_ask: Please delete the restriction on working for others after the agreement ends; the confidentiality clause already protects your information.

Pelanggan tidak bertanggungjawab membayar apa-apa yuran bagi kerja yang sedang dijalankan atau bagi Hasil Kerja yang belum diterima secara bertulis pada tarikh penamatan.

findings.standard: Either party should provide equal written notice, and the client must pay for all work completed up to the date of termination.

findings.title: One-sided notice period for termination
findings.quote: Freelancer boleh menamatkan Perjanjian ini dengan memberi notis bertulis tiga puluh (30) hari kepada Pelanggan, dan hendaklah menyiapkan semua Pesanan Kerja yang sedang berjalan sebelum penamatan berkuat kuasa.
findings.why_risky: You are held to a 30-day notice period while the client can terminate immediately under clause 6.2. You are also compelled to complete all active work orders prior to exiting.
findings.standard: Notice periods should be mutual and equal for both parties, usually 14 to 30 days.

verdict.headline: Agreement contains severe statutory violations including repossession without notice, no rebate on early settlement, and tied insurance.
summary: The contract permits immediate vehicle repossession without notice after a single missed instalment and authorises entry onto premises, which contradicts statutory protections under Malaysian hire-purchase law.
Clause 7.1 denies any rebate of interest charges upon early settlement and prohibits voluntary termination by handing back the vehicle.
The agreement restricts motor insurance strictly to the dealer's insurer and excludes all condition warranties and dealer representations.

findings.title: Daily compounding late fee
findings.quote: If an instalment is not paid when due, a late fee of 0.5% of the overdue amount is charged for each day it remains unpaid. findings.standard: Lenders should charge simple interest or a modest, fixed one-off late fee on overdue amounts, without daily compounding.
findings.suggested_ask: Please delete the daily compounding 0.5% late fee and replace it with a reasonable, non-compounding late charge as permitted by law.
